description: The floating-point numeric literal (ISO §2023:8.3.3.3.3: 'A floating-point numeric literal is formed from two fixed-point numeric literals separated by the letter E without intervening spaces'; the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA spelling 1,5E3 is the same literal, §2023:12.3.7.4 GR14 a) - 1.5E3, -2.5E-2, .5E10 - in every position the lexer produces one (COMPUTE operand, MOVE source, VALUE, relation operand, FUNCTION argument, subscript, SET, CALL argument). A different construct from the floating-point USAGEs (usage-float-short-2002, usage-float-binary32-2014 ...) and from the floating-point numeric-edited PICTURE (pic-external-float-2002), which are data descriptions: the literal needs neither and appears in a program whose data are all fixed-point. COBOL-85's numeric literal is the fixed-point form alone (a literal of at most 18 digits with an optional decimal point and sign). THE EDGE IS DERIVED, NOT QUOTED (VCR row 7.37; the repo holds no 1985, 2002 or 2014 text, ratified decision #1): IBM's Enterprise COBOL Language Reference lists 'Floating-point numeric literals' among its IBM EXTENSIONS - the features it defines beyond the COBOL standards it conforms to, the 85 COBOL Standard first - so the form is not COBOL-85's; none of the 459 NIST CCVS-85 programs writes one; and every conformance case in this repository that writes one is filed at 2002 or later. GnuCOBOL 3.2 has no dialect option for it and accepts it at every -std (silence, not evidence), and IBM's list of the 2002/2014 standard features carries no floating-point-literal row, so the 2002-versus-2014 split is not derivable in-repo and the row takes the provisional 2002 edge rows 7.31/7.36 take - the edge that never refuses a legal 2002 program; a wrong guess costs only an under-reject at --std 2002. Gated position-blind on the TOKEN by LiteralScreen (kb/Work PB674), whose walk covers the unit's tree and every compiler-directive fragment.
